authority: Read-only existing source/artifacts; report writes only under independent-review. No browser, process control, test, build, new agent, product modification or external effect. Root owns adoption, integration, leases and closure.

reanchoring.scope: Continued exact native request after sealed cost r4 review; no restart or replay. Root cost lease active during bounded artifact inspection.
reanchoring.formalGovernorLifecycleCredit: Not claimed; unavailable formal currentness/epoch/JOIN receipts are not invented.

inspection.method: Whole unstripped original stills and selected original JPEGs; sidecar JSON only for sampling and source identity. The 25 fps WebM is not used as an independent source clock. No contact-sheet generation, interpolation, replacement, pixel repair, or earliest-frame classifier.
inspection.selectionCaveat: Near-time samples only: before/after labels refer to recorded native adoption timestamps, not an exact compositor-presentation join. Chromium times use source epoch minus navigationAbsolute; Firefox samples use receipt-relative times with unbounded acquisition latency. Samples do not establish the earliest complete frame or continuity between samples.

supportedObservations: All 18 final records retain current Moon source lineage, matching native/sky generation 0 and Orlando wall scene identity; the recorded phase position bounds remain at or below .0416 device px. Seventeen end with refined-terrain; Firefox clear new-tab ends with unavailable terrain-preview as F1. State is consumer evidence, not first-pixel timing.

Every final ordinary PNG was viewed whole. The 325x530 card, six prayer rows, footer and centered buckle remain present; the Moon is mostly in frame for night/dawn, and no obvious phase/scale/material swap or stars through the Moon disc appeared in the selected whole scenes. This is a sampled observation, not all-phase, mutation-based opacity or continuous-transition certification.

Clear, rain and partial-cloud samples show early Moon and catalogue anchors with later denser full-catalogue appearance. Preview/full metadata bind the same catalogue SHA da5002f0eda9ad3e0f2cc7c95ab423043feea61e8522239d2930ca1945beef2e and a 921-record bright subset. Rain/cloud obstruction is visible and does not itself imply a missing-star failure. Source physics/astrometry correctness is inherited only through its existing exact owner proofs, not newly established by these pixels.

Both moon-negative scenes show a faint dark calendar disc with a thin lit limb, no visible stars through its interior and no surrounding lunar glow; consumed native altitude is about -38.2 degrees and moonlightOpacity=0. Dawn samples show a faint textured calendar disc and twilight without a painted dawn cone/band. Day samples show the daylight corner solar body and UI with Moon/stars appropriately suppressed; absent firstInitial in day is not a zero-render timing sample.

Rain is explicitly model-estimated-wet: code 63/cloud 65/2 mm synthetic preceding-interval amount, visual rain permission true, qualified present-observation permission false, lightning false. The review grants no observed-precipitation or lightning claim.

Chromium sky retry holds the full pack for 20 s, visibly shows Real sky loading then Real sky unavailable in original frames, invokes a separately labelled explicit retry at about 25.015 s, and reaches full sky ready with current refined Moon. Firefox cloud hold is only 10 s; native-data response ends at 10824 ms and full sky is ready by the 15 s read. This is a successful delay case, not the same timeout/retry as Chromium.

Both Moon-missing cases retain current initial-v5 at the 15 s read after injected full-asset HTTP 503; explicit retry at about 25.015/25.016 s returns true and later accepted refined-terrain is current with retryCount=1. Original errors remain. Before/after stills and sampled raw frames show a retained Moon, not an atmosphere-only replacement. Source HTTP failure/retry is supported; decoder, Image or body-stream fault recovery is not exercised by these cases.

Firefox partial-cloud DPR2 uses the actual buckle -> field edits -> #setClose route twice; records and whole PNGs show settings open and closed on target B then new A, generations 0->1->2. Separately labelled programmatic A-B-A uses generations 3/4, +30 min seek advances epoch 12, live return 15, reference withdrawal removes the surface at 16, calendar return restores current initial-v5 at 17. These are post-startup controls; no live DPR-change, stale >30 s or out-of-order completion proof is added.

The original unstripped scenes do not establish a materially changed H1 composition requiring a new owner visual request. The accepted H1 contract remains preserved at frozen product identity. Illustrative layer subtraction cannot substitute for that proof.

findings.observation: Final read at document 123146 ms, acquisition elapsed 131467.99999999348 ms: current=true, visibleSource=terrain-preview, status=unavailable, retryCount=0, error="Moon refinement did not meet the admitted quality criterion". The whole final PNG still shows a Moon and intact UI.
findings.implication: Retained current preview and truthful unavailable status are supported; successful final refinement and all-entry recovery are not. Exit 0 and empty top-level page errors do not override the Moon error.
findings.nextAction: Retain this exact failed refinement in the qualification ledger. Any later repair/retry needs its own bounded decision; this review proposes no new acquisition.

findings.observation: maxFieldDifference is respectively 4.889960596372433 and 3.763980706950513. The helper reconstructs nativeAtmosphereFields, subtracts the derived lunar/natural field from consumed r.linear, and clamps to zero. Its reconstructed background does not equal the consumed skyBackgroundLinear. Current native-preview.mjs retains physicalSkyBackgroundLinear and applies the approved lunar display operator into skyBackgroundLinear/lunarNightDisplayLinear.
findings.implication: No-physical-lunar-field and no-residual-night-field are illustrative interventions, not exact additive component attribution or raw-field-preservation proof. Full/restored ordinary images remain reviewable; CSS removals support only their narrowly observed layer visibility. No claim that the post-H1 recomposition reproduces the ordinary frame.
findings.nextAction: Correct summary scope and retain original diagnostics. No new attribution campaign or product edit is required for this bounded visual review.

findings.observation: Original Firefox rain 000029, day 000032 and Moon-missing 000033 truncate the lower card; clear iframe cold 000035 has a broad white interruption, and 001125 a white horizontal strip. Clear 001131 and later full PNGs show intact layout.
findings.implication: These are contrary original capture observations, not evidence of a uniquely established product/layout or recorder cause. Later stills cannot repair continuous pixel coverage or certify an uninterrupted transition.
findings.nextAction: Retain exact original images and clock limitations; no capture retry is admitted by this report.

acceptanceMapping.S1: OPEN. No new strict timing, earliest-first-frame, gap or matched-baseline PASS. Keep all original failed/uncovered intervals and Firefox capture limitations.
acceptanceMapping.S2: Bounded support for native subset/full catalogue presence under the named rain/cloud/clear conditions and delay cases; no whole S2 first-presentation certificate from samples.
acceptanceMapping.S3: Consumes prior separately sealed compact numerical/isolated visual review only within that scope; these native samples add current displayed-body observations.
acceptanceMapping.S4: Sampled transition evidence only. No obvious sampled swap, but no continuous window, bright-star mutation/fade sweep or full S4 PASS.
acceptanceMapping.S5: Named HTTP 503/explicit retry and sky timeout/explicit retry are supported at exact new records; prior failed Chromium delay r3/r4 are unchanged. Firefox clear new-tab refinement remains failed.
acceptanceMapping.S6: Named actual UI and programmatic controls supported; other mandatory stale/DPR/out-of-order guards require their separate exact evidence.
acceptanceMapping.S7: Direct/generic iframe 390x600 observations supported; full entry/viewport/platform matrix and Firefox actual extension parent remain open. No file or later supplement consumed.
acceptanceMapping.S10: No new H1 implementation/owner request triggered by a demonstrated material composition change; retain approved R0022-L1 ancestry. This is not a new owner acceptance or blanket whole-scene certification.

recommendation: Adopt the bounded observations and three explicit findings. Preserve frozen product and original failures; correct summaries rather than rerun attribution or modify visual source. Integrate later separately scoped entry evidence and measured cost returns before the final candidate-wide decision.
